description:
The Integrated Scheme on Agriculture Cooperation was launched by the Government of India in 2017. 

This scheme was initiated to enhance the agricultural productivity and improve the income of farmers. 

The primary objective is to promote cooperative societies in the agricultural sector. 

The scheme aims to strengthen the cooperative structure in agriculture. 

It also seeks to provide financial assistance and support to farmers through cooperatives. 

The government intends to enhance the capacity of these cooperatives to serve farmers better. 

The scheme focuses on improving the supply chain and marketing of agricultural products. 

It aims to ensure that farmers receive fair prices for their produce. 

The Integrated Scheme on Agriculture Cooperation has a target of increasing the number of cooperative societies. 

The goal is to establish at least 1,000 new cooperative societies by 2022. 

The scheme also aims to increase the membership of existing cooperatives. 

It targets to raise the membership by 20 percent over the next five years. 

The benefits of this scheme include financial assistance for setting up new cooperatives. 

The government provides a grant of up to INR 2 lakh for the establishment of new cooperative societies. 

Additionally, the scheme offers training and capacity-building programs for cooperative members. 

Farmers can also benefit from better access to credit through these cooperatives. 

The scheme promotes the establishment of Farmer Producer Organizations, or FPOs. 

FPOs are intended to empower farmers by providing them with collective bargaining power. 

The government aims to establish 10,000 FPOs by 2023. 

These organizations are crucial for enhancing the income of small and marginal farmers. 

Eligibility for the scheme is primarily based on the farmer's membership in a cooperative society. 

Farmers must be engaged in agricultural activities to qualify for assistance. 

There are no specific age limits for eligibility under this scheme. 

However, farmers must demonstrate a commitment to cooperative principles. 

The application process for the Integrated Scheme on Agriculture Cooperation is straightforward. 

Farmers must approach their local cooperative society to express interest in joining. 

They need to fill out an application form provided by the cooperative. 

Required documents include proof of identity and land ownership. 

Farmers may also need to submit a declaration of their agricultural activities. 

Once the application is submitted, the cooperative society will review it. 

If approved, the cooperative will assist in the registration process. 

The timeline for the application process can vary depending on the cooperative. 

Typically, it takes about 30 to 60 days for the entire process to be completed. 

Disbursement of funds under this scheme occurs in phases. 

Initial grants are released upon the establishment of the cooperative. 

Subsequent funds are disbursed based on the performance and activities of the cooperative. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. 

The National Cooperative Development Corporation plays a significant role in implementation. 

State governments also have a crucial role in facilitating the scheme at the local level. 

Farmers can contact their local agriculture offices for more information. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of technology in agriculture. 

Digital platforms are encouraged for better communication among cooperatives. 

The government aims to integrate technology to enhance productivity. 

This includes the use of mobile applications for market information. 

The scheme also promotes organic farming practices among cooperatives. 

Farmers are encouraged to adopt sustainable practices for better yields. 

The government provides training on organic farming techniques. 

The Integrated Scheme on Agriculture Cooperation is part of a broader initiative. 

It aligns with the National Policy on Cooperatives, which was adopted in 2002. 

The policy aims to promote cooperative societies as a means of economic development. 

The scheme also addresses issues of food security and rural development. 

It aims to uplift the socio-economic status of farmers. 

The government has allocated substantial funds for this scheme. 

For the financial year 2022-2023, the budget allocation was INR 1,500 crore. 

This funding is aimed at supporting the establishment and functioning of cooperatives. 

The scheme has seen positive feedback from various stakeholders in the agricultural sector. 

Farmers have reported increased income due to better market access. 

Cooperatives have also been able to negotiate better prices for agricultural products. 

The scheme has contributed to the overall growth of the cooperative sector in India. 

It has also fostered a sense of community among farmers. 

The government continues to monitor the progress of the scheme closely. 

Regular assessments are conducted to evaluate its impact on farmers' livelihoods. 

The Integrated Scheme on Agriculture Cooperation is a significant step towards agricultural reform. 

It aims to create a robust cooperative framework for farmers across India. 

The scheme is expected to play a vital role in achieving the goal of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

The government remains committed to enhancing the agricultural sector through cooperative efforts. 

This initiative is crucial for ensuring sustainable agricultural development in India. 

The Integrated Scheme on Agriculture Cooperation represents a holistic approach to agricultural welfare. 

It integrates various aspects of farming, marketing, and cooperative management. 

The scheme is a testament to the government's dedication to improving the lives of farmers. 

It highlights the importance of collective action in achieving agricultural prosperity. 

The future of this scheme looks promising with ongoing support and commitment from the government. 

Farmers are encouraged to actively participate in cooperative societies for maximum benefit. 

The scheme is a vital tool for empowering farmers and enhancing their livelihoods.
